name: Congenital Secondary Polycythemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for congenital secondary polycythemia

criteria.description: Sustained increase in red blood cell mass above normal reference range
Normal or elevated serum erythropoietin concentration
Negative testing for JAK2 V617F and exon 12 mutations to exclude polycythemia vera
Positive family history of polycythemia consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Exclusion of acquired causes of hypoxia such as chronic lung or cardiac disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of sustained elevated erythrocyte mass with normal or elevated erythropoietin levels, absence of JAK2 mutations, and exclusion of acquired hypoxia causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for mutations in oxygen-sensing pathway genes (e.g., VHL, EGLN1, EPAS1) may support diagnosis

laboratory: Normal or elevated serum erythropoietin levels
Absence of JAK2 V617F and exon 12 mutations
imaging: Normal chest imaging excluding pulmonary causes of hypoxia
genetic: Mutations in oxygen-sensing pathway genes such as VHL, EGLN1, EPAS1
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Exclusion of acquired causes of secondary polycythemia

distinguishingFeatures: History of chronic hypoxia (lung disease, high altitude)

redFlags: Signs of thrombosis (e.g., stroke, deep vein thrombosis)
Sudden visual loss or retinal vein occlusion
